    Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

    In a recent development, if Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a substantial role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

    Louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

    In a recent development, the fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager stated. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”.

He opens up his body and curls a shot first time towards the far corner, forcing Kepa into the save down to his right.

    Riquelme shoots from just outside the box and forces Kepa into a save down to his right.

    Betis have one goal from a corner and now Arsenal do. Betis keeper Valles complains that he is being fouled by Havertz after Tzolis swung in the corner from the left and the ball comes through to Hincapie, who has the simplest of headers from inside the six-yard box.

    In a recent development, normal service is resumed with a Gunners goal from the corner 👏Piero Hincapié gives the @Arsenal fans reason to celebrate! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/b7h979i0Gv.

    Sources indicate that important block from P Garcia. Dowman cuts in from the right across the face of the penalty area and finds Tzolis in space to his left. Tzolis takes one touch before taking on the shot from inside the Betis box but P Garcia slides in with a crucial block.

    In a recent development, that is quite the finish! Deossa receives the ball in a central position around 25 yards out. He takes a couple of touches before lashing a shot with his left foot. His effort flies into the top corner and Betis have a 2-0 lead. Considering the quality of the finish, I am surprised that Deossa did not celebrate more bearing in mind you do not score screamers like that every day!

    Nelson Deossa...what a hit! 😱😱Real Betis double their lead over Arsenal with a stunning strike and Mikel Arteta doesn't look happy 🌴 pic.twitter.com/4J5QnjOury.

    It has been revealed that since Gyokeres misses that very good chance just a minute into the game, Arsenal have not really carved out many genuine opportunities in front of goal, other than that Tzolis wasted chance. Every time they reach the final third, they are lacking that cutting edge.

    Calafiori’s role is interesting. He’s very nominally a left back but is routinely stepping into midfield and raiding forward, often ending up in positions you’d associate with a No. 10. It’s the kind of role Nico O’Reilly played under Pep Guardiola at Manchester City.

    Recent findings suggest that valles is so, so lucky. The Betis keeper inexplicably passes the ball straight at Tzolis inside the Betis penalty area but Tzolis is unable to capitalise. That is a huge slice of luck for Valles as that was a ridiculous moment.

    Betis have already scored one goal from a corner and they now have another corner after Nwaneri’s clearance behind. The inswinger is sent into a good area but this time Arsenal deal with the danger.

    Arsenal were the better side in the early stages but Betis have grown into this and have taken confidence from that goal.

    The first goal of the night goes the way of the Spaniards. The corner from the left should be dealt with by Kepa but the Arsenal keeper makes an absolute mess of it. The ball goes straight through him and comes to Riquelme at the far post. He takes one touch before firing into the net. Kepa is appealing for a free-kick but there is never a foul in there.

    Real Betis strike first at the Aviva! 🌴Riquelme takes advantage of poor Arsenal defending at the corner to open the scoring 👀 pic.twitter.com/1ubVDayElP.

    Recent findings suggest that that is dire goalkeeping from Kepa. He’s desperately tried to claim he was fouled but he just made a complete hash of it.

    It has been revealed that betis have their first shot of the night. P Garcia receives it out on the right and cuts inside onto his left. The space opens up for him to shoot and he obliges, forcing Kepa into a save before the ball is smashed behind for a corner...

    It has been revealed that calafiori may be on the teamsheet tonight for Arsenal at left-back but when they are in possession the Italian is moving into midfield. Lewis-Skelly, who is playing in the number six role, is dropping in between the two centre-backs when Arsenal have the ball.

    Betis win a free-kick out on the left, with the chance to send it into the Arsenal penalty area for the first time tonight. It is clipped into a good area but Kepa is out of his goal to catch it.

    Arsenal should be ahead one minute into the game with their first attack of the game. Havertz picks up the ball on the corner of the box out on the left and passes it inside to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes one touch before shooting from the edge of the six-yard box but his shot is saved. In reality, Gyokeres should not have given Valles in the Betis goal any chance of saving that one.

    We are under way at Aviva Stadium.

    Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Arsenal led out by Ben White and Betis by former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin, and make their way past the Premier League trophy. We are moments away from kick-off in Dublin.

    Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Hincapie, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Nwaneri; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.

    A special night for Irish Gunners tonight, so who better to describe what @Arsenal means to so many in Ireland than Liam Brady, Emma Byrne and David O'Leary 🔴🇮🇪"It's a class club" 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/Fgi2ztxgLG.

    In the building 🫡 pic.twitter.com/hNITeYh7Gj.

    “When I see the training and how hungry they are for every training drill, that means everybody is ready to compete at the highest level. When you are a player of Arsenal, you compete for every title that is possible. It is not only about the Premier League, it is about all the competitions we are playing for. I see a clear mindset and everything, that everybody is on the same page to win titles here. I saw it from the first training and I think when you train like that in the game, it makes it even better. I came here ready, with my fitness level and I was happy that I could show it here as well. I want to be myself and to show on the pitch all the passion and desire to win because I really like to win games and to give everything.

    Sources indicate that “If I give 100% for every game and every duel, I think who does not like this? I think that is the best thing for a football player, and then you will always have the support from the supporters. I am thinking about how to improve and settle as fast as possible in the club, because I have the opportunity to train directly with the team from the beginning of the season, to play pre-season games and then to go to official games. This is a chance to play directly from the beginning and then it is up to me to show the qualities and what I can bring to the team. I am pretty confident I will show it in the next games.”.

    INS:Illan Meslier ⇠ Leeds, FreeChristos Tzolis ⇠ Club Brugge, £34m.

    Arsenal are closing in on the signing of Newcastle and Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimaraes in a deal worth £75m.     Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

    In a recent development, arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

    Real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

    Sources indicate that they have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

    It's never too early to start looking ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft, right?

    We're at Week 11 the NFL season, and the order for the draft in a few months is already starting to take shape.

    At least for now, the Tennessee Titans have taken over control of the No. 1 pick. That's all thanks to the Los Angeles Chargers, who finally picked up their first win of the season on Monday night in Baltimore.

    The Chargers have joined both the Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins with 1-8 records, but the Titans have the the edge for the top pick due to a weaker strength of schedule.

    Sources indicate that he Chargers sit at No. 2, and the Dolphins are at No. 3. The Newly introduced York Jets and Philadelphia Eagles round out the top five, and the Jets also own the Indianapolis Colts' first-round pick, which slots at No. 6.

    It has been revealed that with several weeks to go in the regular season, there are still several teams in play for the No. 1 overall pick. The Jets and Eagles, both with just two wins this season, aren't out of the question yet, either.

    For now, though, the Titans are in control of that top spot.

    #3359. Industry News: Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

    📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1277 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1277 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The big prize of this free agent class is ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal.
    • There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the signing team is getting a surefire ace for several years.
    • Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The big prize of this free agent class is ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. We've seen and will continue to see predictions that he's going to land a deal of around 8-10 years and topping $400 million. The knee-jerk reaction to such prognostications in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.

    Let's stop right there. I don't think it's all that risky. There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the signing team is getting a surefire ace for several years.

    Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.

    In a recent development, since returning from surgery in 2023, Skubal has been absurdly good. Across his ages 26-29 seasons, he's made 103 starts and has gone 50-20 with a 2.47 ERA (169 ERA+), 0.92 WHIP and 757 strikeouts in 626 ⅓ innings. He's only walked 109, or 1.6 per nine innings. He rarely gets hit hard, he rarely gives up many runs, he strikes out a high number of hitters and rarely walks any. Simply, he's been good at everything.

    The recent track record here notes this is the best pitcher in baseball, at least in the long view (we could argue Paul Skenes was better in 2025 and Jacob Misiorowski was better in 2026, to name two examples, but if we looked at 2023-present, it isn't all that close).

    There isn't a dropoff in the postseason, either. In eight playoff starts, Skubal has a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts against nine unintentional walks in 50 ⅔ innings.

    In a recent development, he's stellar. Pretty much all the time.

    It has been revealed that also, the career workload isn't anything to be concerned about. Skubal heads to his age-30 season now with only 925 ⅓ innings in the regular season. Even counting the playoffs doesn't get Skubal to 1,000 innings at the massive-league level. Let's go back to Skenes. He's only 24 years old and already has 495 career innings. Another ace? Justin Verlander had 1,553 ⅔ career innings through his age-29 season.

    There just isn't a ton of tread on these Skubal tires.

    We'll hear plenty of consternation about Skubal being 30 years old next season as it relates to signing a long-term deal. We'll also hear people say a deal is risky due to his injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in college, flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and arthroscopic surgery (a latest procedure using a Nanoscope) in 2026.

    The simple matter is that pretty much every pitcher nowadays has had some sort of surgery on his arm, notably the elbow, and we've seen pitchers time and again bounce back after elbow surgery to perform at a high level.

    In a recent development, skubal just did it. He only missed roughly six weeks after his procedure this past season. He came back to make 19 starts after the surgery and posted a 2.73 ERA with 141 strikeouts in 115 ⅓ innings.

    Sources indicate that I mentioned Verlander above. Skubal is a multi-time Cy Young winner, so it's acceptable to look at some of the best pitchers in baseball and how they aged into their late-30s in recent memory.

    Again, Skubal will be in his age-30 season in 2027. If he signs an eight-year deal, it'll run through his age-37 season.

    For those so worried about the long-term finances of the team owner who ends up signing Skubal, are you sure you're really worried that he won't be productive through five, six, seven or even all eight years of that deal? Given his track record, talent, pitching arsenal, relatively low workload given his age and how well some of the best pitchers have fared through their mid-30s, he actually seems like a great bet.

    A decade ago, the common talking point was that long and huge deals for pitchers never age well. That isn't actually the case, for the most part. Here are some of the biggest pitcher contracts of all time and how they unfolded (or are unfolding).

    Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers, 12 years, $325 million -- He came over from Japan for his age-25 season, so this one was a different animal. Still, it sure doesn't seem like it'll be a bad deal, does it?

    Gerrit Cole, Yankees, 9 years, $324 million -- Through six years of the deal, Cole has missed a chunk of time due to Tommy John surgery. He's also won a Cy Young, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times, been worth 22.4 WAR and was the ace of an American League pennant winner.

    Stephen Strasburg, Nationals, 7 years, $245 million -- Here's the bust. Strasburg was never healthy again after the 2019 World Series title run. Still, the Nationals wouldn't have that title without him.

    Justin Verlander, Tigers, 10 years, $219.5 million -- This was the deal that ran from 2010-19. During this deal, Verlander won two Cy Youngs (one in the second year of the deal, one in the final year), a World Series, three pennants, 160 games and led the league in pitcher WAR three times.

    Max Fried, Yankees, 8 years, $218 million -- It's only been two years, but Fried is 24-10 with a 2.83 ERA and finished fourth in AL Cy Young voting in his first year.

    Recent findings suggest that david Price, Red Sox, 7 years, $217 million -- He won a World Series in the third year of the contract. Overall, he was 53-26 with a 3.78 ERA (118 ERA+) through the course of the deal.

    Corbin Burnes, Diamondbacks, 6 years, $210 million -- Burnes had his first year of the deal interrupted by Tommy John surgery. He had a 2.66 ERA through 11 starts prior to the injury. The jury's still out, but he heads to his age-32 season fully recovered now.

    In a recent development, zack Greinke, 6 years, $206.5 million -- Over the course of this deal, Greinke was 77-39 with a 3.55 ERA (125 ERA+) and 19.9 WAR. He had a fourth-place Cy Young finish in there.

    In a recent development, CC Sabathia, 9 years, $202 million -- The Yankees won the World Series in Sabathia's first year there and he started the deal with three straight top-four Cy Young finishes. Overall, during this deal, he was 120-73 with 27.1 WAR and had five straight 200-plus inning seasons.

    Industry observers note that max Scherzer, 7 years, $191.4 million -- During this contract, Scherzer won two Cy Youngs, a World Series title and 99 games with a 2.75 ERA. He posted 41.8 WAR. In the seven years on this deal, Scherzer finished in the top five in Cy Young voting six times, with 2020 being the outlier.

    Recent findings suggest that we can close with this. Some people might not care for such a measure, particularly the salary cap crowd who will be worried about the owners paying too much. Regardless, let's stick with the general belief that each individual WAR (1.0 WAR) is worth a bit over $8 million per season.

    By this measure, Skubal was worth $48.4 million in 2024, $53.7 million in 2025 and $41.7 million last season. Putting aside how much less money he actually made than what he was doing on the field, and knowing everything laid out above, I'll ask a simple question:.

    Are you sure a 10-year, $400 million deal for this guy would be a "risk?".

    I think we could argue that it would be a bargain.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Dopo aver respinto gli assalti estivi di Brentford, Parma e Fiorentina su richiesta di Gattuso, la dirigenza biancoceleste valuta il prolungamento oltre il 2027.

    Il futuro di Matteo Cancellieri alla Lazio continua ad attirare l'attenzione in vista dei prossimi mesi. Secondo quanto riportato da TuttoMercatoWeb, il club deve riflettere con attenzione sul contratto dell'esterno italiano, visto che l'accordo attuale scadrà il prossimo 30 giugno 2027.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    Sources indicate that nel corso dell'ultima sessione di mercato estiva, diversi club avevano provato a sondare il terreno per assicurarsi il giocatore. Dall'estero si era fatto avanti il Brentford dalla Premier League, mentre in Serie A avevano preso informazioni prima il Parma e poi la Fiorentina, specialmente dopo l'approdo nella Capitale di Albert Gudmundsson. Tuttavia, a bloccare ogni possibile partenza è stato lo stesso allenatore Gennaro Gattuso, fermamente intenzionato a non ridurre ulteriormente le opzioni a sua disposizione nel reparto offensivo.

    Il tecnico punta forte su di lui anche per gennaio. Nonostante qualche guaio fisico, Cancellieri ha trovato spazio ed è stabilmente nelle rotazioni, alternandosi con un Isaksen in grande forma. Ora tocca al presidente Claudio Lotito e alla dirigenza decidere se avviare le trattative per il rinnovo.

    MLB rumors: Phillies OF on the trading block, Blue Jays eye ex-Yankee, plus Mets, Mariners, Braves, Rays, more

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1257 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that thursday marks the final day of the General Manager meetings in Las Vegas.
    • Rumors are always fun, so let's round up the latest right here in addition to any news.
    • In a recent development, we have one of our first major-league deals of the offseason as the Braves have signed reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that thursday marks the final day of the General Manager meetings in Las Vegas. Though we haven't seen any major moves this offseason, we have seen an uptick in rumors in the past few days and that isn't a coincidence. Put a bunch of reporters and front-office execs in the same area for three or four days and chatter picks up, even if there isn't a ton of actual substance behind it.

    Rumors are always fun, so let's round up the latest right here in addition to any news.

    In a recent development, we have one of our first major-league deals of the offseason as the Braves have signed reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal. Phillips ranked No. 34 on our top 50 free agent list.

    It has been revealed that phillips, a 32-year-old right-hander, has been a setup man or closer for the Dodgers for the last several seasons. In returning from surgery last season, he appeared in 31 games, pitching to a 3.46 ERA and 1.07 WHIP with 33 strikeouts in 26 innings. The majority of his closing experience came in 2023 when he had 24 saves in 27 chances.

    The Braves' closer last season was Raisel Iglesias, but he's a free agent. Holdover Robert Suarez could take over those duties while Phillips, lefty Dylan Lee and youngster Didier Fuentes are also in the late-inning mix.

    The Blue Jays went from one of the best offensive teams in 2025 to one of the worst in 2026. They'd love a big bounceback from Vladimir Guerrero Jr., among other positive movements, but they also look for outside help. Might that help come in the form of free agent infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr.?

    The Jays have met with representatives for Chisholm, reports Sportsnet.

    Chisholm, 28, hit .231/.312/.399 last season, but had a huge 2025 and any signing team would be hoping for the 2025 version of Chisholm.

    The Jays do have a capable incumbent second baseman in Ernie Clement, but either Clement or Chisholm can be used in the outfield and the Blue Jays certainly need outfield upgrades.

    The Phillies have been telling opposing teams that they are not "locked into anything" regarding their current outfield situation, according to The Athletic, so much so that All-Star outfielder Brandon Marsh is available in a trade.

    As things stand, with Bryce Harper moving back to first base, the Phillies would have Bryan De La Cruz in right, Justin Crawford in center and Marsh in left, but that all seems pretty fluid as they look to upgrade the ballclub and keep that window of contention open.

    Marsh, 28, had a stellar start last season, leading to his first-ever All-Star Game. Through July 1, he hit .319/.352/.530. The rest of the way, however, he slashed .177/.241/.241, dragging him down overall to a 90 OPS+ and 0.4 WAR on the season.

    The Mariners have shown interest in free agent left fielder Ian Happ, per MLB Network.

    Happ, 32, has spent his entire 10-year MLB career with the Cubs, who drafted him in the first round all the way back in 2015. He was pretty consistent from 2022-25, averaging 3.9 WAR with a .251/.347/.433 (118 OPS+) line and winning four Gold Gloves. Last season, though, he dipped to .218/.326/.412 (103 OPS+) with 2.7 WAR. He still topped 20 home runs for the fifth time in the last six years.

    The Mariners have a vacancy in left field with Randy Arozarena having hit free agency and a need to upgrade their offense.

    Yesterday's substantial news was the Yankees' interest in free agent first/third baseman Alec Bohm and The Athletic reports that we can now add the Mets to the list of suitors.

    Bohm hit .249/.315/.383 (87 OPS+) with 15 home runs, 88 RBI and -0.2 WAR last season. It might be surprising to see him garnering such interest on the open market, but there isn't much right-handed power out there and Bohm finished last season strong (.318/.402/.453 in his last 42 games). The Mets, meanwhile, are desperate for help at the cold corner after last year's disastrous Jorge Polanco experiment. Jared Young did provide a glimmer of hope at first base before suffering a concussion in September while colliding with a teammate on a play.

    Free agent starting pitcher Dustin May has a decent market right now, according to MLB Network, with at least the Cubs, White Sox, Padres and Astros having shown interest in the right-hander.

    Recent findings suggest that may, 29, made 31 starts between the Cardinals and Brewers last season, going 7-9 with a 4.70 ERA in 145 ⅔ innings. He indicated flashes of brilliance with the Cardinals and had a stretch from April 10 to June 15 during which he posted a 2.54 ERA in 12 starts, but in the end there was plenty of inconsistency and even bad, forcing him into a bullpen role in the playoffs for the champion Brewers.

    Free agent catcher Ryan Jeffers has been extended the qualifying offer from the Twins, meaning he has to decide by net Tuesday whether to accept the one-year, $23.15 million contract or hit free agency. There's nothing that notes a team can't re-sign a player after he declines their qualifying offer, of course, and it sounds like that path is possible in this case.

    Jeffers will decline the QO and the Twins are interested in reaching a multi-year deal to bring him back, reports the Minnesota Star-Tribune. Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 with 14 home runs for Minnesota in 2026, a standout line for a catcher, though he missed several months with a broken hamate. The Twins do have several catchers in their farm system, including Vahn Lackey, the No. 3 pick in last year's draft, and Eduardo Tait, who headlined the trade return for Jhoan Duran.

    Much has been stated and will continue to be said about the 2027 free agent class and how it looks relatively weak, especially on the position-player side, where the best players are the likes of Jazz Chisholm Jr., Seiya Suzuki, and the aforementioned Arozarena and Jeffers.

    As we know, the Rays love to find avenues where they can exploit market inefficiencies. Their latest move might be to hit the trade market with center fielder Jonny DeLuca in anticipation of moving Victor Mesa Jr. to center, according to The Athletic.

    Industry observers note that deLuca, 28, got more playing time than ever before in 2026, appearing in 112 games and getting 370 plate appearances. He hit .266/.300/.429 (101 OPS+) with 11 homers, 50 RBI, 17 steals and 1.7 WAR.

    Industry observers note that fresh off a playoff berth despite the lowest payroll in all of baseball at a paltry $75ish million, the Guardians are planning to increase payroll. Or so they say.

    Sources indicate that "We'll go up," club president Chris Antonetti told The Athletic. "We have to.".

    The Guardians hosted six playoff games and made some money there, not to mention that they have a bunch of players hitting arbitration and surely they want to spend more to remain competitive. There's an added wrinkle here, too, which would be that the ownership side is really pushing hard for a salary cap when the upcoming CBA expires in a few weeks. With a cap comes a floor and we've seen MLB float proposals with salary floors in the $180 million range, or well more than double what the Guardians had last season.

    So, yeah, I'd say the Guardians "have to" increase payroll, one way or another.

    • Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.
    • Sources indicate that bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

    Sources indicate that bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

    According to recent reports, just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side revealed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

    Industry observers note that aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

    Stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR.

    Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

    Possession: Aston Villa 44%-56% Bayern MunichShots: 8-16Shots on target: 3-8Corners: 3-7.

    Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

    The final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

    Victory in the final match of the #AudiFCBTour! 💪🔥 pic.twitter.com/UFhQhme62i.

    The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

    It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

    There will be four added minutes.

    It has been revealed that when Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

    Recent findings suggest that gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

    Industry observers note that for 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

    Maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

    Abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

    Boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

    Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

    Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

    Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

    In a recent development, A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

    Recent findings suggest that bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

    Bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

    Unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

    That is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

    It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

    Vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

    Should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

    Just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

    Good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

    Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

    Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

    Tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

    It has been revealed that bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

    We are back under way in Hong Kong.

    Possession: Aston Villa 45%-55% Bayern MunichShots: 4-7Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 1-2.

    The first half in Hong Kong is brought to an end and Bayern take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Kim’s goal.

    There will be one added minute at the end of this first half.

    Industry observers note that aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

    Industry observers note that the German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

    According to recent reports, that is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. He drives through the Villa half and at the penalty area but his pass outside looking for Cardozo is poor and overhit, with the ball rolling out for a goal kick. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

    It has been revealed that bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

    Sources indicate that the first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

    Recent findings suggest that that was lovely from Pavlovic. The German midfielder reveals good feet to beat Gomes before getting his shot away from a central position just outside the box. He forces Bizot into a decent save but one he should be making.

    Bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

    Sources indicate that bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown is starting at left-back for Bayern today with Saibari not involved as he closes in on a return from a knock picked up at the World Cup with Morocco. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

    It has been revealed that aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is currently out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

    The ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

    Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

    Good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

    The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

    The first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

    It has been revealed that interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

    Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

    It has been revealed that chelsea and Juventus played in this stadium the other night and it is safe to say that the pitch does not look in the best state ahead of kick-off today. It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

    Sources indicate that right now, before the two sides emerge, the crowd in Hong Kong are being treated to some pre-match dancing and entertainment, which includes people dressed as pandas and sharks dancing. Would the Premier League ever take inspiration and have dancing pandas before kick-off?

    Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Kamara, Joao Gomes, Hemmings, Buendia, Guessand, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Abraham, Nedejkovic, Bogarde, Rowe, Burrowes, Carroll, Lynch.

    Recent findings suggest that bayern Munich: Neuer, Kim, Tah, Brown, Boey, Laimer, Bischof, Pavlovic, Ibrahimovic, Binder, Cardozo. Substitutes: Ulrich, Podar-Stiube, Urbig, Kimmich, Luis Díaz, Palhinha, Ito, Chávez, Pavic, Bara, Manuba, Stanisic, Della Rovere, Assomo.

    The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return to training after their World Cup exploits and Aston Villa are also without captain John McGinn and new signing Alejandro Garnacho, who picked up knocks in their win over BG Pathum the other day.

    In a recent development, aston Villa have already sold Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers this summer, with Lucas Digne on the verge of a move to PSG, but could another starter be on the way out of Villa Park? England defender Ezri Konsa has been linked with moves to the likes of Arsenal and Liverpool but will Unai Emery be able to keep hold of the 28-year-old?

    The atmosphere is building with our fans in Hong Kong! 🔴⚪️#AudiFCBTour pic.twitter.com/m4fFXAWxGb.

    It has been a big summer of change at Aston Villa already and there could be more changes before the end of the window. Left-back Lucas Digne is set to move to PSG and is set to be replaced by Atlético Madrid’s Matteo Ruggeri. Joao Palhinha, who is on the bench for Bayern Munich today, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa.

    “Aston Villa are a top side with a very good coach. They have a large squad and will field plenty of talent. They have already played more friendlies than us, but for us it is a good challenge. It is a match in which we will learn a lot about our team’s fitness. It will be a good match for us.”.

    It has been revealed that “It is difficult to improve; after all, it is not just about the trophies we have won, but also about the number of goals and matches we have won.     Rays third baseman Junior Caminero finished in second. At age 22, he played all 162 games, leading the Rays to the best AL record. He hit .276/.360/.524 (144 OPS+) with 42 home runs, 101 RBI and 100 runs, posting a 5.7 WAR. He's already made history, too, as the Rays had previously never had a player finish in the top five of MVP voting.

    It has been revealed that houston Texans quarterback CJ. Stroud passed for 194 yards and three touchdowns, providing more than enough offense for a defense that shut down the Indianapolis Colts effectively in a 26-3 win on Thursday night.

    The Texans won at home for the first time this season after losing their previous five at Reliant Stadium.

    Sources indicate that stroud completed 21-of-27 passes with one interception. A second one appeared to be taken away in the second quarter before replay review ruled that Colts safety Cam Bynum didn't catch the ball cleanly.

    According to recent reports, nico Collins caught three passes for 58 yards and a touchdown, while Kayshon Boutte followed with two catches for 40 yards and a score. Rookie tight end Marlin Klein caught Stroud's third TD pass.

    Sources indicate that the Texans' offense also benefited from the return of running back David Montgomery, back after a four-game absence due to a groin injury. The eight-year veteran rushed for 107 yards on 26 carries, keeping several drives moving on the ground. Emari Demercado also ran effectively, gaining 33 yards on five carries.

    However, the sharpest thing seen on the field Thursday night may have been the Texans' "Rivalries" alternate uniforms that harkened back to the Oilers' classic look. With the victory, Houston improved to 4-6 and stayed on the fringes of the playoff race in the AFC. The Texans play host to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 12.

    Industry observers note that on the other side, the Colts could get nothing going with their rushing attack. Jonathan Taylor managed only 21 yards on 11 carries. That put more pressure on Daniel Jones to produce in the passing game, which did not happen.

    Recent findings suggest that jones completed 12-of-27 passes for 144 yards and an interception. He did connect on four passes of 20 yards or more, but that simply wasn't enough to move Indianapolis toward the end zone. He was also tackled for a safety by Will Anderson Jr. in the third quarter after the Colts were pinned at their 5-yard line on a 62-yard punt from Houston's Kai Kroeger.

    Anderson now has 11.5 sacks this season, tops in the NFL, after notching a career-high 12 last season.

    With just under eight minutes left in the game and the Colts trailing by 23 points, Colts coach Shane Steichen replaced Jones with Anthony Richardson. But he threw two incompletions on his first series, the only action he saw.

    Sources indicate that naturally, Steichen was asked if the Colts will make a quarterback change for their next game. "We'll evaluate everything," he said.

    Altogether, the Colts generated only 167 yards of total offense. Anthony Gould tallied 48 yards receiving on two receptions, followed by 30 yards and two catches from Ashton Dulin. Taylor had four catches, but only for six yards.

    Even kicker Spencer Shrader couldn't provide many points, missing two of his three field-goal attempts. One of those kicks was from 62 yards and was blocked.

    Indianapolis has lost six of its past seven games, dropping to 3-8 for the season. Yet four teams have worse records in a subpar AFC. Up next for the Colts is a home matchup with the Fresh York Giants (5-3-1).

    A very topical reference for the winning graphic:.

    That was a dominant win in all facets for Houston, which improves to 4-6 to keep its slim playoff hopes alive.

    The Colts fall to 3-8 and further into the abyss.

    On his final rush of the game, Montgomery goes for 14 yards to get his total to 107 yards on 26 carries today.

    Anthony Richardson didn't do much better for the Colts, throwing two incompletions on his first series and rushing for 2 yards.

    Indianapolis might have something cooking on its latest possession. Daniel Jones hits Anthony Gould for a 17-yard gain to the Houston 43-yard line.

    Houston adds to its lead with a safety and touchdown in the third quarter for a 26-3 lead over Indianapolis, and this game is going to the final 15 minutes.

    #3341. Now with an MVP, Pete Crow-Armstrong is on the path for an all-time great career. Where could he stack up?

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1120 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Now with an MVP, Pete Crow-Armstrong is on the path for an all-time great career. Where could he stack up?

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1120 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The MVP winners were revealed Thursday evening and, unsurprisingly, the runaway unanimous winner in the National League was Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs.
    • Crow-Armstrong had an all-time great regular season, which is what the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America award honors.
    • Sources indicate that so what's next?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The MVP winners were revealed Thursday evening and, unsurprisingly, the runaway unanimous winner in the National League was Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs.

    Crow-Armstrong had an all-time great regular season, which is what the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America award honors. He hit .280/.372/.570 with stellar defense, led the league in home runs (tied with Kyle Schwarber) and massively upgraded his on-base skills. Now, just a few months shy of his 25th birthday, he has an MVP to his name.

    Sources indicate that so what's next? To answer that, we'll look backwards.

    Since integration, only eight center fielders have posted at least 8.0 WAR in a season age-25 or younger: Willie Mays, Mickey Mantle, Willie Davis, César Cedeño, Ken Griffey Jr., Andruw Jones, Mike Trout and PCA. The only ones to top PCA's 9.8 were Mays, Mantle and Trout. If we went back to pre-integration, Tris Speaker and Ty Cobb were the only others who bested PCA here.

    What road map will PCA's career follow?

    Industry observers note that willie Davis was an inconsistent hitter through his age-23 season but had flashed a nice power-speed combo. Sound familiar? That gaudy 8.4 WAR total in 1964, though, was driven largely by monster defensive metrics. Davis hit .294/.316/.413 (110 OPS+) with 23 doubles, seven triples, 12 home runs, 77 RBI, 91 runs and 42 steals. There's little doubt that PCA's 2026 season dwarfed this one overall, and Davis was far behind Mays (11.0) for the league lead in WAR.

    Recent findings suggest that for the rest of his career, Davis averaged 3.1 WAR per season, and though he had good years, he never reached 6.0 WAR again. The WAR figure was, again, mostly driven by defense. He had several good offensive seasons, but his only 20-homer season came in 1962 when he was 22, two years prior to his career year.

    Davis' career probably looks a lot like PCA's apparent upside before his home run barrage in the first half of 2025. He racked up over 60 career WAR with a decent batting average, excellent defense and excellent baserunning.

    With PCA reaching 30-30 last year and 40-40 this year, though, the bar has been raised.

    César Cedeño followed up his 8.0 WAR season with a 7.4 season at age 22 and 5.8 at age 23. He was very good through age 29 and, in fact, the most statistically similar player through both ages 27 and 28 was Hall of Famer Carl Yastrzemski. Things fell apart after that. As a quick and easy way to illustrate it, Cedeño amassed 49.4 WAR through his age-29 season and only 3.6 in his final six years.

    It's easier to remember that Andruw Jones' career unfolded in similar fashion because we witnessed it not too long ago and then discussed his Hall of Fame candidacy during his nine turns on the ballot before he finally made it in. In Jones' 12 Braves' season, he racked up 368 home runs, 1,117 RBI and 61 WAR while generally being considered the best defensive center fielder in baseball. Once he left, in time for his age-31 season, Jones accrued just 1.7 WAR in his last five seasons.

    Through Jones' age-28 season, the most statistically similar players are Bryce Harper and Frank Robinson.

    To compare these two to Crow-Armstrong, the argument would be that he'll continue to look like one of the best players in baseball -- even if taking steps backward from being the very best in the 2026 regular season -- before falling apart once he's around 30 years old.

    According to recent reports, certainly possible, but given the adjustments he's already not only been willing to make at the plate, but eager to make, I'm just not seeing him all of a sudden hitting a wall. Sure, at some point he'll start losing speed and that'll affect his defensive range and baserunning, but why would the plate skills deteriorate all of a sudden?

    Then again, few saw it coming with Jones.

    All three of these players were on the path to having an argument as the best player in history before injuries derailed them in their 30s and left them as mere "all-time greats.".

    Through Mickey Mantle's age-30 season, he had 90.7 WAR. He averaged 121 games per year in his final six seasons, putting up 19.5 WAR. Through  Ken Griffey Jr.'s age-30 season, he had 76.2 WAR. He played 10 more seasons, but only amassed 7.6 more WAR. Through Mike Trout's age-27 season, he had 72.1 WAR (his top statistical similars were Mantle, Robinson and Griffey). We'll skip 2020 for obvious reasons, but since then he's averaged 90 games and 3.0 WAR per season.

    Industry observers note that even with the drop-offs, it would be surprising to see Crow-Armstrong reach this level because it's surprising to see any player reach this lofty standard. In career WAR among center fielders, Mantle is fourth, Trout is fifth and Griffey is sixth. They trail only Cobb, Speaker and the guy we're going to discuss next. Joe DiMaggio is seventh.

    Despite the lofty standard PCA set for himself in 2026, coming close to Willie Mays' career would be jaw-droppingly shocking, and that is absolutely not intended as a slight.

    Sources indicate that mays has an argument as the greatest player in baseball history and he put himself in that discussion by being good at everything and doing it all with great longevity. From his age-23 to -35 seasons, he led the majors in WAR eight times, leading the NL an additional two times. His worst seasons in that timeframe were 7.6 and 7.8 WAR. In that span, he also led the league in runs twice, hits once, triples three times, home runs three times, stolen bases four times, average once, on-base percentage once, slugging percentage five times and OPS five times.

    Recent findings suggest that mays even posted 5.2 WAR at age 39 and 6.3 at age 40. He led the NL with a .425 OBP when he was 40 years old! He hit .345/.411/.667 at age 23.

    Mays' 156.2 career WAR ranks third among position players all-time behind two guys you might have heard of: Barry Bonds (162.8) and Babe Ruth (162.3).

    I feel pretty strongly Pete Crow-Armstrong isn't headed for a run at this career and that's just fine.

    In a recent development, the realistic long-term range for the 2026 National League MVP seems somewhere between Cedeño and Mantle. It's a wide variance of outcomes between those two, obviously, as well it should be when the player we discuss is only 24 years old. For his name to be mentioned among these at all is a testament to the year Crow-Armstrong just put together.

    After Thursday's loss, will Colts give Anthony Richardson another real shot?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Down 26-3 to the Houston Texans Thursday night, the Colts made a quarterback change, benching Daniel Jones and bringing in Anthony Richardson for mop-up duty in the blowout loss.
    • According to recent reports, the Colts took this approach late in the 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Nov.
    • Richardson, 24, has been in limbo for a few years now, a gifted talent in a state of arrested development, playing for a team that doesn't appear too jazzed to get a longer re-examination of a player they drafted fourth overall just three years ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Down 26-3 to the Houston Texans Thursday night, the Colts made a quarterback change, benching Daniel Jones and bringing in Anthony Richardson for mop-up duty in the blowout loss.

    According to recent reports, the Colts took this approach late in the 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Nov. 1, giving Richardson a few token snaps. It wasn't an evaluation; it was a cup of coffee. That was his last appearance prior to Thursday.

    Richardson, 24, has been in limbo for a few years now, a gifted talent in a state of arrested development, playing for a team that doesn't appear too jazzed to get a longer re-examination of a player they drafted fourth overall just three years ago.

    On Thursday, Richardson entered midway through the fourth quarter and missed his first two throws of the night. There was no second series; the Texans ran out the clock. And it almost feels like the Colts are trying to run out the clock on Richardson, Jones, Riley Leonard — all of it.

    Head coach Shane Steichen this week remarked he takes "everything into account" when it comes to the quarterbacks. He added: "Obviously, the biggest thing is taking care of the football moving forward.".

    Asked about a potential QB change after Thursday's loss, Steichen said, "we'll evaluate everything.".

    Steichen previously has been reluctant to put all the blame on Jones, and it's fair to point out that the Colts offloaded two notable talents at the trade deadline in offensive guard Quenton Nelson and wide receiver Josh Downs.

    It has been revealed that but the problems have been chronic, even when those player were on the roster. Jones hasn't had more touchdowns than interceptions in any game this season. He's thrown picks in 10 of his 11 games. The contract extension he signed in the offseason is looking more painful, on the books for $46.8 million next season, although it's a deal the Colts can get out of as a post-June 1 cut.

    Still, if we're already forecasting the potential end of Jones in Indianapolis, and likely another pivot at quarterback for the franchise, why is Richardson not even a provisional option at this point? Is he that far gone in their eyes?

    The excuse for not making a change this week was the Thursday game and the shortened schedule. But it's not as if Richardson hasn't been here for a minute. It's hard to imagine Steichen sees a whole lot of upside in Richardson, or the hook would have come sooner for Jones. Heck, it wouldn't be stunning if Steichen gave Leonard a chance, even over Richardson, at some point.

    The Colts declined Richardson's fifth-year option, so the writing has been on the wall for a bit. It's hard not to look back at that 2024 game when Richardson reportedly "needed a breather" as a turning point in Steichen's trust in the QB, even if he ended up bringing Richardson back a few weeks later. Whenever that turning point happened, the trust level just hasn't been there for some time.

    Steichen has hinted that a QB change could come, even prior to Thursday night. So there could be an opportunity for someone. There are six games remaining, with the Week 13 bye upcoming.

    But isn't Steichen worried about his job? The general manager is already gone, and the owner is watching the operation closely. Outside of a narrow home win over the Dolphins, it hasn't looked very pretty lately. Steichen is going to do what he feels he needs to do to keep his job.

    Sources indicate that is there any upside to bringing Jones back next week against the Giants? The Colts might not believe in Richardson, but they could end up helping each other out. If the QB can string a few games together, it helps his chances elsewhere next season. And if the Colts can win a few games, maybe everyone won't lose their jobs.

    The substantial picture isn't pretty, and the Colts still don't have a first-round pick next year, but it's hard to imagine they can't try to squeeze something out of a player who at least has made some energy-generating plays with his legs, even if Richardson's passing metrics haven't been terribly defensible.

    Beggars can't be choosers. Jones is playing like a guy who's less than a year removed from an Achilles injury, and the Colts' roster has been gutted. Sure, Leonard is the QB who might have the best chance to return next season, but Richardson has the better talent.

    Can he get one more shot to do something in Indy?

    As NFC South threatens another sub-.500 division winner, does NFL playoff structure need makeover? 'It'll take an egregious deal'

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Entering Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season, clubs find themselves asking what's become a familiar question: Will this season's NFL playoff bracket actually feature the NFL's best teams?
    • The NFC South is trending dangerously close to fronting a sub-.500 division winner for the second consecutive year and third time in five years (the 4-5 Carolina Panthers at the moment lead the division).
    • The discrepancy leaves some in the league questioning the eight-division playoff structure that has stayed relatively consistent since 2002.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Entering Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season, clubs find themselves asking what's become a familiar question: Will this season's NFL playoff bracket actually feature the NFL's best teams?

    The NFC South is trending dangerously close to fronting a sub-.500 division winner for the second consecutive year and third time in five years (the 4-5 Carolina Panthers at the moment lead the division). Across the conference, three NFC West and all four NFC North teams each stand above .500. If the playoffs started this week (they don't), the 6-4 Seahawks and Rams would each miss out.

    The discrepancy leaves some in the league questioning the eight-division playoff structure that has stayed relatively consistent since 2002. For the first 20 years of that reign, only three teams won a division without winning at least half of their games (two more finished 8-8). Since the league expanded its regular-season schedule to 17 games in 2021, the frequency of sub-.500 teams hosting wild-card games has ticked up.

    Recent findings suggest that "What makes the disparity worse in the last five years for sure is that we've added another [regular-season] game," one source with knowledge of league playoff proposal debates told Yahoo Sports. "The more you add games, the more separation in the standings you get.".

    And with the league's determination to add an 18th regular-season game by the next collective bargaining agreement (the NFLPA would have to agree to any schedule expansion), the disparity could only worsen.

    What will factor into league decisions on whether to amend the playoff structure in the coming years, or in concert with the addition of a possible 18th game? Yahoo Sports surveyed high-ranking league sources to better understand the debates from recent annual meetings as well as the most likely factors to motivate any changes.

    Sources were split on whether they wanted any shift to the structure — and how that shift should materialize if it does unfold.

    One high-ranking NFC executive who favors revamping the playoff structure was skeptical anything will change in the next five to 10 years, even if the schedule expands to 18 games.

    "I think it'll take an egregious deal," the executive told Yahoo Sports. "It'll take freaking someone winning the NFC South with seven wins and somebody coming in with like 12 wins. It'll take something like that, and it'd probably take an influential owner to be on that 12-win team.".

    Would the NFL ever consider eliminating divisional favoritism altogether in favor of seeding a conference purely by record?

    "I think the appetite for that is zero.".

    Those in favor of maintaining the playoff-structure status quo cite the value of divisional excellence.

    From a practical standpoint, 14 of a team's 17 regular-season matchups are identical to those of their division foes. Every team plays six in-division games, four teams from another division in their conference and four teams from a division outside of their conference. The remaining three opponents reflect a team's record the prior year. That means ranking teams within a division eliminates most of the strength-of-schedule variance that exists between divisions.

    "Strength of schedule is usually the most accurate predictor of teams who are good or bad," a second high-ranking NFC executive told Yahoo Sports. "At the end of the year when you look at who the surprise teams are, and you look at their strength of schedule, I promise you their strength of schedule is weak.".

    Added a high-ranking AFC executive: "It gives every group of four the same opportunity.".

    On a more emotional note, rewarding divisional wins with a top-four seed and a home playoff game puts a premium on the value of winning intradivisional games. Rivalries rage more strongly as the stakes rise. The geographic proximity between many division rivals contributes to the heightened tenor.

    "It's good for fandom, it's good for the game, it's good for television," the first NFC executive remarked.

    Each of these concerns has reached the NFL annual meetings, from 2008 and 2009 proposals withdrawn after split votes from the competition committee to more recent proposals at the 2023 and 2025 NFL annual meetings.

    In 2023, the Chargers proposed seeding wild-card teams higher than division champions when the division champion 1) finishes below .500 and 2) has lost four or more games than a wild-card team.

    In 2025, the Lions proposed more broadly to seed wild-card teams higher than division champions when wild-card teams finish with better records.

    Excerpt from a presentation at 2025 NFL owners meeting debating the Detroit Lions' playoff proposal.

    Sources indicate that neither proposal dared to suggest a division winner shouldn't clinch a playoff spot. But each questioned whether struggling division winners deserved to automatically host a playoff game.

    The proposals failed to generate sufficient support to pass.

    Sources indicate that sources in favor and opposed to shifting the reward toward record alone admitted: Playoff formulas that dive into the minutiae of counting win discrepancy between division winners and wild-card advancers could complicate and decrease fan interest in predicting playoff brackets. Determining the exact threshold of a change is controversial, too. Multiple sources surveyed for this story mentioned how Tom Brady and the New England Patriots' success was undoubtedly helped by playing in an otherwise-weak AFC East during his tenure. But no team influences the strength of its own division, nor the divisions it's selected to play that year.

    "More often than not, it's not a direct correlation that, 'Oh, you got 12 wins, you're better than the 10-win team …'" the first high-ranking NFC executive said. "It gets dicey to try and figure out something that's 'fair' for everybody and passes the smell test, because there are some divisions that the teams are better, and I can acknowledge that.".

    Clubs admitted during the 2025 meeting discussions that the current playoff formula has limitations, a source present for those discussions told Yahoo Sports. But teams overwhelmingly felt the current playoff structure fit the current schedule format better than the alternative.

    A high-ranking AFC executive who believes in the current playoff format questioned the itch for change.

    According to recent reports, "There's too many people in our league that want to change rules every year and change formats," the executive said. "We have a divisional structure and that is the first benchmark. … I think the history of it is the way it should be.".

    In the 2024 NFL season, Jared Goff and the Lions won a high stakes NFC North battle against the Vikings that decided the division on the final day of the regular season.

    When the league debated Detroit's proposal last year, a presentation weighing the merits touted four main benefits, per a copy obtained by Yahoo Sports:.

    The end of the regular season would be more competitive.

    The end of the regular season could draw more fan interests, better ticket value and better TV ratings.

    The postseason would be more equitable.

    The chance of a conference's two best teams playing in the conference championship (rather than a wild-card or divisional-round game) would increase.

    The main drawback cited: decreasing the incentive to win a division.

    Sources indicate that the emphasis on late regular-season competition reflected what could be a key force in any eventual postseason shift. As the regular season has grown already to 17 games, with discussions of 18 on the horizon, the chance to secure playoff spots with multiple weeks left to play grows. The league's current requirement that all regular-season finales feature divisional games already guarantees a handful of lopsided divisions in which at least one team has nothing to gain by winning. Sometimes, a game features a division winner with no playoff movement possible and a desire that a divisional opponent wins to hurt the opponent's draft position. Starters increasingly rest during regular-season finales.

    "When you add an 18th game, there's a lot of consequences …" the league source who was present for the playoff proposal discussions noted. "[As] teams get further apart in the standings and in terms of draft order and playoff seeding, it leads to a last week of the season that may also require other changes in terms of incentives for playoff qualification or the draft.".

    These conversations could go hand-in-hand with determining the formula for a potential 18th game. At that schedule size, divisional games would account for just one-third of a team's schedule. With 12 non-divisional opponents to play, each team could, in theory, play all three other divisions in its conference if the league sought to level the strength-of-schedule playing field within the NFC and AFC brackets.

    In a recent development, "Now, that goes against the NFL's whole notion of trying to create parity," a high-ranking NFC executive mentioned. "The NFL wants bad teams to play a bad team so someone gets a win so that every year they can say four or five fresh teams make the playoffs. I think that is really valuable.".

    The league already expanded the playoff bracket from its 30-year run of 12 teams to 14 in 2020.

    For now, the league will turn its eye toward the cellar-dwelling NFC South and the not-far-ahead NFC East to see how poorly the worst playoff participants will finish this season.

    After that? Expect conversations to continue to simmer, while also expecting momentum for change to remain slow in a league that values tradition and divisional competition.

    Industry observers note that "I don't think you can change anything until you have a more balanced schedule," the high-ranking NFC executive reiterated. "Winning your division means that the teams that played the closest facsimile of the schedule of yours, you are better than. That deserves a home game.

    "Nobody's sitting here talking about the Giants having played [among] the weakest strength of schedule and having a winning record and getting a home game. So to me, until teams all play a balanced and fair schedule, the playoff format is really a waste of time from a discussion standpoint.".

    Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

    📅 10 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (614 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Newly introduced York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team unveiled on Saturday.
    • Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position.
    • Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Newly introduced York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team unveiled on Saturday.

    Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

    Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

    According to recent reports, the 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

    It has been revealed that shesterkin was a major reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

    Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

    New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

    First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

    It has been revealed that newly introduced York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

    The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a massive commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

    Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and Fresh York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

    Recent findings suggest that however, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

    Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether Newly introduced York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

    In a recent development, chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

    The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

    The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

    Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

    The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

    Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.
