    #3281. 10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1651 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1651 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that this Friday, Nov.
    • Sources indicate that dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary.
    • Recent findings suggest that with that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that this Friday, Nov. 20, is an important date on MLB's offseason calendar. It is the deadline for teams to offer 2027 contracts to their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players. The player does not have to sign by Friday's 5 p.m. ET deadline, but he must be offered a contract. If he's not, the player is considered non-tendered and immediately becomes a free agent.

    Sources indicate that dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary. Adolis García, Nathaniel Lowe, Alek Manoah, and Christopher Morel were among the notable non-tenders last offseason. Go back a few years and significant names like Cody Bellinger and Kyle Schwarber were non-tendered.

    Recent findings suggest that with that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors. You can be sure these teams will scour the trade market for these players and try to get something back before making the non-tender official.

    Projected salary: $11.1 million (team control through 2028).

    Duran was a non-tender candidate even before the Jake Bauers signing pushed him out of the everyday lineup. There is no such thing as too many good players, but the Red Sox now have two first basemen (Bauers and Willson Contreras) and four outfielders (Duran, Wilyer Abreu, Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela). Mickey Gasper and Masataka Yoshida are still around too. That's eight players for five lineup spots (first base, DH, three outfield spots). On any given day, three of those guys will be on the bench. Duran, who got MVP votes in 2024, had a 20-20 season in 2026, but it came with a ballooning strikeout rate and a .266 on-base percentage. He has been on the trade block for close to two years now and the writing is on the wall. If the Red Sox are unable to trade Duran this week, there's a real chance he'll get non-tendered Friday given his hefty salary projection.

    Projected salary: $7.7 million (team control through 2028).

    It has been revealed that former No. 1 overall draft picks have been non-tendered in the past (Tim Beckham most recently), just not by the team that drafted them. Non-tendering Torkelson would be a tough look for the Tigers even though he has not developed into the impact hitter he was projected to be coming out of Arizona State. Simply put, the salary is beginning to outweigh the production. Torkelson, 27, is a 25-30 homer bat with one of the league's highest strikeout rates, middling on-base percentages, and no secondary value (defense, baserunning, etc.). That mentioned, the Tigers do not have an obvious replacement first baseman ready to step in (Colt Keith was the backup in 2026). That, plus the fact that Torkelson has No. 1 pick pedigree, could keep him in Detroit another year.

    Projected salary: $2.3 million (team control through 2029).

    According to recent reports, the American League Rookie of the Year in 2024, Gil has battled injuries and ineffectiveness in the two seasons since. The swing-and-miss rate on his fastball went from an elite 28.5% in 2024 to a below-average 18.8% in 2025 and 17.4% in 2026. Gil, 28, spent time in Triple-A this past season and the Yankees moved him into the bullpen late in the year, where the results were so-so. The salary projection is a pittance, particularly for a team with New York's payroll, though Gil is now out of minor-league options (he must pass through waivers to go to Triple-A) and doesn't have an obvious role. Because he is a pitcher and breathing, and also has a major award win in the not-too-distant past, the Yankees might be able to find a trade partner this week. If not, Gil is a definite non-tender candidate.

    Projected salary: $7.6 million (team control through 2028).

    A fan favorite and an All-Star this past season, Clement crashed hard in the second half, and the fact of the matter is he has a .295 on-base percentage in his three full seasons with the Blue Jays. Also, the soon-to-be 31-year-old's defensive numbers tumbled this year. Clement's contact skills are elite and he's a versatile, high-energy player. As a utility guy, he's an ace. As an everyday player, he's stretched. Clement's projected salary is hefty for a utility player, particularly one with limited offensive upside who no longer reliably catches the baseball. My guess is the Blue Jays will keep him and live with the salary, but it's not an obvious decision.

    Projected salary: $5.1 million (team control through 2028).

    In a recent development, similar to Torkelson, non-tendering a former No. 1 overall pick would be a tough look for the Twins, but a clean break might be best for all involved at this point. Lewis, 27, has trended down since his boffo second half in 2023, enough that he was sent to Triple-A for a spell this summer. He's also moved down the defensive spectrum from third base to first base. It's not due to a lack of effort; Lewis is a major tinkerer who has tried all sorts of swing adjustments. It just hasn't come together. A fresh start elsewhere, away from the spotlight of former No. 1 pick and face of the franchise, might be best for him. The budget-conscious Twins could then reallocate the projected $5.1 million elsewhere on the roster. Right now, they can't count on Lewis to hit or have a meaningful impact defensively.

    Projected salary: $3.4 million (team control through 2028).

    It has been revealed that in 2023, Gorman slugged 27 home runs and looked like one of baseball's top young power hitters. In the three seasons since, he has not come close to repeating that success. The hope was that moving him to third base, his natural position, would unlock Gorman's offense following the Nolan Arenado trade. That didn't happen, and Gorman spent a substantial chunk of the summer in Triple-A, where he continued to have a hard time making contact. Now 26, Gorman has a minor-league option remaining and can go to Triple-A again in 2027, but the signs are not subtle. The Cardinals are reportedly seeking a stopgap third baseman until top prospect Jesús Báez is ready, which would likely not be the case if they had any belief in Gorman. That projected $3.4 million salary is a high price for a reclamation project ticketed for the minors.

    Projected salary: $6.9 million (team control through 2028).

    Recent findings suggest that right-handed power is in short supply throughout baseball and Burger, 31 in April, has hit at least 28 home runs in three of the last four years. He is a one-tool player, though. The home runs come with low batting averages, low on-base percentages, higher-than-average strikeout rates, and little to no defensive or baserunning value. Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young remarked his team lacked "grit and toughness," whatever that means, and indicated he wants more hitters who grind out at-bats. That's not Burger, who can hit the ball a mile but is not known for making life tough on pitchers. The $6.9 million projection could be deemed too pricey for a player with such a limited skill set.

    Projected salary: $6.6 million (team control through 2027).

    Doval went from the Yankees to the Pirates at the trade deadline, then from the Pirates to the Giants on waivers in September. He's a former All-Star who led the National League in saves in 2023, two things that have boosted his arbitration salaries. Since 2023, Doval has been a middle reliever who was on the outside of the Circle of Trust™ more often than not. The 29-year-old righty still throws very hard. There's nothing wrong with his arm. It's hard to believe he gets hit as hard as he does sometimes. Doval earned $6.1 million in 2026 and a player cannot have a salary cut by more than 20% during his team control years. That would set Doval's minimum 2027 salary at $4.88 million. I wonder if the Giants would offer him a pay cut, say $5.5M or so, and tell him it's either that or a non-tender. That happens a few times a year around the league.

    Projected salary: $6.5 million (team control through 2027).

    A fan favorite in San Diego -- "Ho-ly Sheets!" chants are commonplace during his at-bats at Petco Park -- Sheets has fallen by the wayside a bit with the Padres, so much so that he started just one of their six postseason games this year. The 30-year-old is a platoon player who is good against righties more than great and is a defensive liability at both first base and left field. Realistically, Sheets is a platoon DH, and teams rarely pay well for that role unless they're confident they will get substantial offensive numbers. In the grand scheme of things, the projected $6.5 million isn't much. It is top-of-the-market dollars for this skill set, however.

    Projected salary: $1.4 million (team control through 2029).

    Two years ago, Blanco threw a no-hitter in his eighth career start. This year, he was so far out of the picture that he pitched once in Houston's last 12 games (two innings at the end of a 13-2 blowout), and the Astros opted to start Peter Lambert on two days' rest with a postseason spot on the line in Game 162. Blanco, who is older than you may realize (he turned 33 in August), returned from Tommy John surgery this summer and had a rough go of it. The pitching-needy Astros could send him to Triple-A next season, as he has a minor-league option remaining, but his stuff was diminished after surgery, and again, they didn't trust him late in the year. You would be surprised at how many cheap pitchers get non-tendered every year. Blanco could join them this week.

    It wouldn't shock me if ... for Week 11: New WR crashes OROY race, Jared Goff's pesky streak continues

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1536 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the beauty of the NFL is its unpredictability.
    • For instance, last week we accurately put you on to both Zach Charbonnet and Josh Downs making waves that far surpassed their over/under gambling odds.
    • This go-around, we turn our attention to a couple of individual performances, as well as highlight some developments in the playoff and award races that we wouldn't be shocked to see unfold in Week 11.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the beauty of the NFL is its unpredictability. It's what keeps us coming back each Sunday, as we never quite know what's going to unfold. We might have a good idea, but more often than not, the consensus outcome fails to actually come to fruition. As difficult as it may be to try and predict what's around the corner in a given week, we've done a pretty good job this season of predicting the unpredictable.

    For instance, last week we accurately put you on to both Zach Charbonnet and Josh Downs making waves that far surpassed their over/under gambling odds. We also told you to temper your expectations regarding Fernando Mendoza's first career start, which proved wise. Of course, we're not going to bat a thousand here given the nature of trying to see into the future, and we came up short in our predictions that Brock Purdy would ascend as the MVP favorite, along with Will Anderson Jr. falling two sacks shy of matching his single-game career high.

    This go-around, we turn our attention to a couple of individual performances, as well as highlight some developments in the playoff and award races that we wouldn't be shocked to see unfold in Week 11.

    All NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.

    Recent findings suggest that tony Pollard spent the first five seasons of his career in Dallas after the Cowboys selected him in the fourth round out of Memphis in 2019. The veteran back left the organization in 2024, inking a three-year, $21.75 million deal with the Titans. Now, for the first time since leaving the Cowboys, Pollard will face his former team on Sunday.

    The 29-year-old has a fantastic opportunity to get one over on his former team, which has struggled immensely to stop the run this season. In fact, the Cowboys are giving up 154.1 rushing yards per game on a 5.2 yards-per-carry clip this season, both the most in the NFL. Dallas is also giving up the third-most receiving yards to running backs and the most receiving touchdowns.

    This sets Pollard up for a dominant day out of Tennessee's backfield and continues what has been a white-hot stretch for him. Over his past three games, Pollard has rushed for 279 yards (5.1 yards per carry) and five touchdowns, while catching 14 of his 17 targets for 112 yards and another score.

    The way both Pollard and the Cowboys' run defense are trending, it wouldn't surprise us at all if he logs 150 scrimmage yards.

    According to recent reports, gambling nuggets to note: Tony Pollard's O/U rushing yards prop for Week 11 is 65.5 (-110 to the Over). Meanwhile, Pollard's O/U rushing + receiving yards prop for Week 11 is 87.5 (-110 to the Over).

    It has been revealed that the Lions enter Week 11 with a 7-2 record, which is good for first place in the NFC North and slotted in as the No. 2 seed in the conference. Amid the team's five-game winning streak, however, Jared Goff has been a little loose with the football. The Lions quarterback has thrown four interceptions over his last three games, including two last week against the Patriots in Germany.

    Goff has thrown an interception in three straight games entering Sunday's contest with the Buccaneers, and it really should be four straight games. Before this streak started, Goff had two interceptions dropped by Packers defenders in Detroit's Week 7 matchup against Green Bay.

    Now, Goff faces a Tampa Bay defense that will not only be well rested after being on the bye in Week 10 but has a knack for snatching interceptions. The Buccaneers lead the league with 16 interceptions. Their 72.7 passer rating allowed is also second-best in the NFL and only looking up to the Vikings, so this has the potential to be a tough task for Goff to overcome. It also sets up a strong possibility that this pesky interception streak will continue.

    Gambling nugget to note: Jared Goff is +122 to throw at least one interception in Week 11.

    It has been revealed that the Cleveland Browns get to kick their feet up and watch the action unfold across the league this weekend as they're currently on the bye. Before the break, the club vaulted into the AFC playoff picture and currently sits as the No. 7 seed with a 6-4 record. Even with Cleveland not playing this week, there's a strong opportunity for the franchise's playoff position to strengthen.

    Namely, they'll be rooting for the Eagles, who host the Steelers (currently the No. 6 seed). If Philadelphia pulls off the home upset over Pittsburgh (who hasn't won a road game against the Eagles since 1965), the Steelers would draw even with Cleveland with a 6-5 record. Because these teams split the season series, the next tiebreaker would be their record within the AFC North. The Browns (2-1) have a better division record than the Steelers (2-2) at the moment, so they'd leap ahead of them.

    On top of the Eagles, if the Panthers and/or Broncos pull off wins against the Ravens and Raiders, respectively, that'd further create some breathing room for Cleveland. By the time they emerge from their bye week and gear up for Week 12, I wouldn't be surprised if the Browns are the No. 6 seed.

    Gambling nugget to note: An Eagles, Panthers, Broncos moneyline parlay is +468.

    It has been revealed that the Vikings have been the talk of the NFL for the bulk of the season thanks to their lethal defense, but they also got a massive boost right before the trade deadline by acquiring Kirk Cousins. The veteran quarterback provided immediate dividends in the club's Week 10 win over the Packers at Lambeau Field, and will try to continue this storybook return to Minnesota when they take on the 49ers in Mexico City. The Vikings are a 3-point underdog in this matchup, but their defense certainly gives them a shot to pull off the upset.

    In a recent development, not to mention that Brock Purdy is 0-2 against the Vikings in his career. In those games, Purdy's teams have averaged just 17 points per game, while he's thrown two touchdowns and committed four turnovers. If Minnesota forces Purdy to look like that once again, they are live to pull out the win.

    Sources indicate that provided they do, Minnesota suddenly has an opportunity to leap to the No. 1 seed in the NFC by the end of Sunday. Of course, that result is contingent on other factors playing out over the course of the slate, but it's not out of the realm of possibility. All the Vikings would need is for the Buccaneers to upset the Lions, dropping Detroit to 7-3 on the season. Then, if Minnesota beats the 49ers to move to 8-2, they leap up atop the division and, because of the newly acquired head-to-head tiebreaker, would jump over San Francisco as the top seed in the conference.

    Sources indicate that gambling nuggets to note: Vikings are +130 to beat the 49ers. The Buccaneers are +270 to beat the Lions. A Vikings and Buccaneers moneyline parlay is +751. Presently, the Vikings are +450 to finish the season as the No. 1 seed.

    According to recent reports, the tightest award race in the NFL amongst players is Offensive Rookie of the Year. Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza is the current favorite, and he's started just one game so far this season. While that speaks to the value of the quarterback position, it also highlights just how wide open the race is and how a player can burst onto the scene midseason and make a legitimate run.

    In that same vein, folks should start paying attention to Saints rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson.

    The No. 8 overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft had the first half of his rookie season erased due to a hamstring injury he suffered during the summer. However, Tyson returned to the field in Week 9 and has almost instantly started making an impact. Over two games, Tyson has been targeted 18 times and hauled in 15 catches for 110 yards. That includes an 11-catch, 80-yard showing last week against Carolina.

    Industry observers note that those receptions are tied for the most in the first two games of a career in Saints history. According to Pro Football Focus, Tyson joined Malik Nabers (2024) and Puka Nacua (2023) as the only receivers since 2020 to have at least 10 receptions in a game within their first two games played.

    Industry observers note that with New Orleans' running game nonexistent and pass-heavy game scripts projected for the rest of the season, Tyson is set up nicely to put up some eye-popping numbers, especially if he's going to command about nine targets per game. That includes this week, when the Saints are 11.5-point underdogs to the Bears. That suggests they'll be playing from behind and will need to throw the football, which could continue to showcase Tyson.

    This might be the time to buy his Offensive Rookie of the Year stock.

    Gambling nugget to note: Jordyn Tyson is +1800 to win Offensive Rookie of the Year.

    • Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era.
    • It has been revealed that just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

    Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

    It has been revealed that just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

    Industry observers note that kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

    It's crucial to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

    Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

    Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

    In a recent development, we already know the Wild are massive-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

    Recent findings suggest that however, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

    Recent findings suggest that with Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

    In a recent development, it was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.

    According to recent reports, carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

    Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

    Sources indicate that utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

    Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

    Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

One team that has "registered interest" in adding Murray is the Phoenix Suns, per Chris Haynes.

    It has been revealed that "From what's going on INSIDE, this sounds like someone hit you to say this!!" Murray wrote in a now-deleted tweet. "THE 'SABOTAGE' IS REAL!!".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.
    • In a recent development, the full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman.
    • As a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.

    In a recent development, the full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman. Newcomers to the ballot are in bold.

    As a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class. Those who get at least 5% of the vote can remain on the ballot the following year, and so on, for a maximum of 10 voting cycles. Players who are on the ballot for 10 years without getting 75% of the vote, in addition to players not getting 5% of the vote, fall off the ballot in ensuing years, though that doesn't mean the doors to the Hall are permanently shut.

    Sources indicate that the results will be announced on Jan. 19, with the induction set for Cooperstown over the summer.

    Here's everything else you need to know about the Baseball Hall of Fame this offseason.

    Sources indicate that as alluded to earlier, there are two different votes each offseason. The BBWAA vote is for former players who have been retired from Major League Baseball for at least five years. It's the most common method in mainstream Hall of Fame ballot discussions. When you hear stuff like "first-ballot Hall of Famer," it means via the BBWAA vote.

    Players who don't make it via the BBWAA vote can get extra chances via committees. That's how, for example, Jeff Kent made it last year. Formerly called the Veterans Committee, the Hall of Fame now uses Era Committees, which are divided into two categories: contemporary baseball (1980 to present) and classic (prior to 1980). The contemporary ballot is then split into two, one for players and one for non-players like umpires, executives, pioneers and managers.

    Sure enough, this time around, it is a non-player Contemporary Baseball Committee, which looks at "managers, umpires and executives whose most significant career impact was realized since 1980.".

    In a recent development, we'll dive further into this group as we get closer to the Dec. 6 vote.

    It has been revealed that giants legend Buster Posey joins the ballot, and he's one of those cases where I don't think a bunch of people need to delve deeply into his numbers. More than statistics, sometimes we get "feel" guys, as in, you just know he's a Hall of Famer. Posey qualifies there, I would think, for 75% of the electorate. We'll obviously do a deeper dive in the coming weeks, but even without the longevity component (Posey only played in parts of 12 MLB seasons), I think he's in.

    In a recent development, as for the rest of the first-timers, the best case would be Jon Lester. Given the way a lot of similar starting pitchers have been treated in voting in recent years, my hunch is he'll be able to hang around on the ballot, but he has a major uphill battle in order to get in.

    Then you're looking at Brett Gardner, Ryan Zimmerman, Kyle Seager, the short peak of Jake Arrieta and relief work of Andrew Miller. Good players worth mentioning, of course, but they won't sniff the Hall and it seems likely all behind Posey and Lester are one-and-dones on this ballot, as they'll fall short of 5% of the vote.

    This is the sixth year for Alex Rodriguez on the ballot, which means it's the sixth time that I point out that we don't really need much time to go over his case. His numbers say he's one of the 10 best position players of all time, but his ties to PEDs are keeping him out to this point.

    Recent findings suggest that he did rise from 37.1% of the vote in 2025 to 40% last time, a new high-water mark. The progress is too modest to believe it's trending toward him getting in, but the number this year is certainly worth watching. If he somehow makes a leap to the 50% range, a deeper conversation might be in order.

    Sources indicate that while some voters don't mind sending in blank ballots to prove some sort of nebulous point, most impose limits on themselves. Whether it's the actual rule of 10 or some voters saying they'll only vote, for example, for a maximum of three players on any given ballot, relatively weak ballots can leave openings for the best players to show huge gains. With Carlos Beltràn and Andruw Jones getting in last year and only one strong first-year candidate, perhaps Chase Utley can benefit.

    Utley is only in his fourth year on the ballot, but he's already made significant gains:.

    According to recent reports, he only needs to add 15.9 points after jumping nearly 20 last voting cycle. The situation is ripe for Utley to either get all the way in or get close enough to where he probably makes the Hall of Fame in 2028.

    Some of us are pushing to lower the Hall of Fame standard on modern starting pitchers, given the decreases in workload and how it affects their career numbers. We might be making some headway, but it's still tough sledding. Here are the holdover starting pitchers and their standing:.

    According to recent reports, the bar for relievers to make the Hall of Fame is justly pretty high. We recently saw Billy Wagner make a late move and make it in his last try on the BBWAA ballot. Francisco Rodríguez has had four chances on the ballot and gotten between 7.8% and 11.8% of the vote thus far.

    In a recent development, K-Rod ranks sixth all time in saves and has good rate stats. He's worth tracking as it relates to three active relievers. Kenley Jansen is third in saves with a similar number of innings pitched to K-Rod. Craig Kimbrel is fifth and has more than 100 fewer innings pitched. Aroldis Chapman is ninth and in the ballpark of Kimbrel in workload to this point.

    If K-Rod continues to have trouble making headway toward induction, does that mean Kimbrel and Chapman will have trouble as well? What about Jansen?

    In a recent development, who else is back on the ballot? A quick look:.

    Posey is a lock. If the committee era chooses Bochy, Baker and/or Sabean, that would be some nice San Francisco flavor, too, right? I'll predict that committee ballot at a later date, though.

    I'll also say Utley's good roll here continues with a relatively weak ballot (at least when you factor in what the PED stain has done to some guys).

    On the player side, my 2027 Hall of Fame class prediction is Buster Posey and Chase Utley.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that there is nothing more valuable in the NFL than rostering a star quarterback on a rookie contract.
    • Sources indicate that to make the most of the opportunity, though, that quarterback must be a legitimate standout.
    • Recent findings suggest that teams with slow-developing or underperforming young quarterbacks face the other side of this equation: the frustration of having enough cap space to field stars at other positions while lacking serviceable play at the most key position of all.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that there is nothing more valuable in the NFL than rostering a star quarterback on a rookie contract. The financial flexibility that comes with a highly affordable signal-caller cannot be overstated. That's partly why the Fresh England Patriots made a run to the Super Bowl last year and why the Chicago Bears are poised to do the same in 2026.

    Sources indicate that to make the most of the opportunity, though, that quarterback must be a legitimate standout. Drake Maye was nearly the league MVP a year ago. Caleb Williams is in contention this season. They and a few others are in line for massive contract extensions when they become eligible.

    Recent findings suggest that teams with slow-developing or underperforming young quarterbacks face the other side of this equation: the frustration of having enough cap space to field stars at other positions while lacking serviceable play at the most key position of all. In many cases, this results in the quarterback's career flaming out and the team looking back to the draft for another swing at finding the face of the franchise. A couple of squads might see that play out in the months to come.

    Below are grades for all 12 starting quarterbacks who are on their rookie contracts.

    Sources indicate that in just his second year as a pro, Maye achieved two feats that no other player on their rookie contract can boast. In fact, in reaching the Super Bowl and finishing one first-place vote shy of the MVP award, Maye stepped closer to glory than most quarterbacks in the league have at any point in their career regardless of contract status. Regression in his third season has come in the form of immense turnover complications (he's tied for second-most through 10 weeks with 13) and a .500 record, but some of that can be attributed to the Patriots roster being depleted by injuries. Speaking of which, Maye's season might be over because of the ankle injury he sustained in Munich in Week 10.

    It has been revealed that the step backward in 2026 and the ankle problem cast uncertainty over what Maye's next contract will look like if he signs one when he becomes eligible for an extension this offseason. But there is no doubt that he is the locked-in quarterback of the present and future for the Patriots. His proven upside is greater than that of any other signal-caller on a rookie deal.

    It has been revealed that the blame for the Houston Texans' underwhelming campaign cannot be directed at C.J. Stroud. While his inconsistency in 2024 and 2025 capped the team's success, his performance this year is the only thing keeping the Texans even remotely competitive in the postseason hunt. His return to the tremendous form that made him a standout rookie has been a pleasant development and puts him in line for a massive payday.

    When he won the Offensive Rookie of the Year award in 2023, Stroud led the NFL in passing yards per game and interception rate. His numbers this season in both of those categories (273.6 ypg, 0.9 INT%) are almost identical to the ones that put him at the top of the league.

    When the Texans inevitably sign Stroud to a lucrative extension, they will bet that the campaigns bookending his four-year career are more indicative of what is to come than the two in the middle.

    Through 26 games, it remains unclear whether Cam Ward is a viable long-term starter in this league. The Tennessee Titans will have a tough decision to make at the end of the year: draft another quarterback or add pieces around Ward when they make four selections in the first two rounds? The second-year surge they hoped would come from last year's No. 1 pick has not arrived, so their patience is about to be put to the test.

    Given that they are actively deconstructing the roster by trading Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker at the trade deadline, it is clear the Titans prioritize developing their young players over making desperation moves to make the roster competitive as right now constructed. That, along with their willingness to keep Tony Pollard and routinely add talent to the wide receiver group, suggests they want to give Ward every opportunity to improve. The next eight games will go a long way in determining whether Tennessee should stick to that plan or seek another option on draft day.

    No team has been more prolific at winning one-possession games since 2025 than the Denver Broncos, and much of the credit goes to Bo Nix. He led the league in game-winning drives last year with seven and leads in both fourth-quarter comebacks (five) and game-winning drives (six) in 2026. Of course, it would be preferable if Nix helped put enough points on the board over the first three quarters that he did not need to pull off heroics in the final minutes, but at least he continues to deliver when his back is against the wall.

    This season is thus far the least productive of Nix's three-year career by completion rate, success rate, yards per game, and passer rating. Some of that regression might be attributable to the offensive coordinator change, which prompted Sean Payton to reclaim play-calling duties in Week 5. What is promising is that Nix's last three games were arguably his best of the campaign, so he might be rounding back into form just in time for the stretch run.

    Sources indicate that even with a slow start to the year, Nix has been everything the Broncos need since he joined them in 2024. And if not for his ankle injury last postseason, he might have played in the Super Bowl. There is no reason to think Denver will not invest in him when the time comes.

    It will take more time to accurately gauge Fernando Mendoza's outlook as an NFL starter. His debut, as should be expected, had its ups and downs. He took six sacks, completed a modest 17 of 29 passes, but scored his first touchdown on a 10-yard run to the end zone. In all, it was a milquetoast showing against a daunting Seattle Seahawks defense.

    The Las Vegas Raiders need to bolster their wide receiver group in the months to come in order to give Mendoza the requisite weapons to succeed. The tight end tandem of Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer should help the No. 1 pick get his feet wet, though.

    Recent findings suggest that J.J. McCarthy might be saving his career in real-time. The inability to stay healthy and the lackluster play when he was on the field during his first two seasons with the Minnesota Vikings made him an undeniable bust -- so much so that the Vikings demoted him to the No. 3 line on their depth chart and moved on from him for pennies on the dollar when the Upcoming York Giants came calling for a trade earlier this year. With the change in scenery, however, has come marked improvement.

    McCarthy's Giants debut was astounding: A 243-yard fourth quarter. Since he earned the starting job, he has completed 66.3% of his passes for 224 yards per game with a touchdown and an interception. He went 2-1 in those starts. That is not half bad for someone who joined the team five weeks into the season. There are still obvious flaws in his game, but McCarthy has helped the Giants maintain their lead in the NFC East so far, and that is about all they could have asked for when they traded for him.

    Industry observers note that the best-case outcome for McCarthy the rest of the way is that he proves himself as a starting-caliber talent and latches on somewhere else in 2027. This is Jaxson Dart's team when he returns to full strength next year. Perhaps the most likely scenario is for McCarthy to settle in as his backup, continue to develop and cement himself as one of the NFL's best No. 2s. That would still be a disappointment considering he is a former No. 10 overall pick, but it would be a step forward from where he began the year.

    Elbow dislocations and a couple of minor lower-body injuries halted Jayden Daniels' momentum in the wake of a remarkable rookie season in which he won Offensive Rookie of the Year, finished seventh in MVP voting and took the Washington Commanders to the NFC Championship Game. He has been proficient when healthy since then, but he has only played 14 games since 2024, and the Commanders are just 4-9-1 even with him in the lineup over the last two seasons. His career thus far is a mixed bag, including the highest highs for a rookie quarterback and the lows of a middling team.

    According to recent reports, the elite rushing prowess that helped him lead the NFL in success rate as a rookie has regressed a bit, but he is a more accurate passer who this year paces the league in interception rate and who is on track to set a career high in yards per game. Again, there is give and take.

    If the Commanders can upgrade their offensive line and increase their depth behind the injured Terry McLaurin at wide receiver, Daniels would finally have enough help around him to potentially take Washington back to its 2024 heights and solidify himself as a top-tier quarterback. He is not the problem in Washington.

    Recent findings suggest that williams and the Bears are on a steep ascent to the top of the league. Individually, Williams is on a trajectory that may one day lead him to an MVP award. And from a team perspective, his climb into stardom is the catalyst behind the Bears' surge toward the front of the Super Bowl race.

    The four-interception debacle in his last outing was an aberration in what has otherwise been a breakout season for the third-year quarterback. Prior to the setback, he indicated an increased comfort in Ben Johnson's high-octane offense and took care of the ball about as well as anyone. Even after that showing, this is the best version of Williams the NFL has seen, with his career-best passer rating, uncanny sack avoidance, and 257.7 passing yards per game.

    It feels like this is the start of a superstar career.

    From Weeks 1-5, Bryce Young emerged as a dark-horse MVP candidate. The second quarter of the season brought him back down to Earth. In totality, this is still by far the best year of his career, and it could not have come at a more crucial time as he approaches a pivotal offseason in which the Carolina Panthers must decide whether to pick up his fifth-year option, sign him to an extension or begin a separation process.

    According to recent reports, coach Dave Canales seems to have a deep understanding of Young's abilities and how best to use them. Young has done nothing but improve under his tutelage. His down weeks are still problematic, but when he is on, Young has been the best version of himself this year. Take his yardage numbers, for instance: the 266.3 yards per game the Heisman Trophy winner averages this season are far greater than the 188.2 of his previous career-best campaign.

    Recent findings suggest that young's development has been a slow burn, but it has been linear and remains on the right track. This is a quarterback Carolina can keep building around.

    It has been revealed that the Latest Orleans Saints' motto is to air it out, and they have a quarterback who can do that. Coach Kellen Moore put a lot on Tyler Shough's plate over his first 18 starts and, thus far in 2026, tasked him with throwing the third-most passes per game at 38.1. Across that hefty workload, Shough turned in a middle-of-the-pack passer rating, which is commendable for a quarterback in his sophomore professional season.

    It has been revealed that if the Saints had a better defense, they would probably stand tall atop the NFL's worst division, and the conversation around Shough would be more positive. Instead, he is merely keeping New Orleans somewhat afloat in a division that could feature a sub-.500 champion. As he continues to build a connection with prized rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson and maintains a highly productive link with Chris Olave, it will become clearer whether he is a true franchise quarterback. But over two half-seasons as a starter, his early returns as a second-round pick are quite positive.

    The stop-and-start nature of Michael Penix Jr.'s three-year career makes it hard to judge fairly. He cannot be faulted for his torn ACL last year and the Atlanta Falcons' questionable management of the quarterback room the year prior. What is up for grading, though, is what Penix has done on the field, and over 20 starts, it is an average-to-slightly-below-average performance.

    It has been revealed that with all of the star talent on the Falcons offense, the team needs its quarterback to perform at a high level and get the most out of Bijan Robinson and Drake London. As they enter the prime of their careers, it is paramount that Penix makes strides. The franchise cannot afford to let its two greatest assets go to waste. In that sense, Penix's slow development is a problem. But at the same time, his flashes suggest that there is a franchise quarterback in him. Back-to-back three-touchdown games in October were emblematic of the ceiling that made him worthy of a first-round pick.

    The arm strength Carson Beck lacked in his final year of college is back. The further removed he gets from his UCL injury at Georgia, the more he looks capable of playing in the NFL. But that does not mean he will thrive as the Arizona Cardinals' starter in the second half of the season, nor does it mean the team should not draft a quarterback with its 2027 first-round pick. Beck was dreadful in Week 10 in his debut, throwing a pair of interceptions, taking five sacks, and losing 34-6 to the Los Angeles Rams. Then again, what third-round rookie would thrive in his first career start, with a depleted wide receiver group and against a top-10 defense?

    It has been revealed that arizona will do its due diligence in the coming weeks to see what it has in Beck. More likely than not, it does not have a franchise quarterback.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.
    • The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.
    • Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

    The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

    Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

    But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

    The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

    Industry observers note that ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

    Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

    Sources indicate that arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

    As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

    Champions 🏆 pic.twitter.com/c0IVLYu3fB.

    It has been revealed that arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

    Arsenal: Kepa (Meslier 46); White (Julienne 78), Mosquera (Ogunnaike 78), Gabriel (Salmon 60), Calafiori (Hincapié 60); Lewis-Skelly (Vieira 78), Havertz (O’Neill 78), Odegaard (Nwaneri 33); Dowman (Ibrahim 78), Gyokeres (Jesus 78), Tzolis (Martinielli 78). Substitutes: Setford, Nelson, Kabia.Booked: Gabriel.Goals: Nwaneri (54), Gyokeres (69 pen).Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson (Yamamoto 91), Inácio (Prates 59), Bensebaini (Reggiani 78), Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha (Guirassy 60), Mane; Karetsas (Chukwuemeka 46), Beier (Sabitzer 59), Silva (Albert 59). Substitutes: Drewes, Lerema, Kabar, Riedl.Goals: Inácio (7), Karetsas (29), Gadou (58).

    Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

    The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

    Sources indicate that meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

    Sources indicate that we have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

    A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

    He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

    It has been revealed that another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

    There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

    Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

    Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

    Sources indicate that right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

    According to recent reports, arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

    The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

    There will now be a penalty shootout.

    There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

    Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

    Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:.

    It has been revealed that with just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

    Sources indicate that the Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

    Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

    According to recent reports, nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

    In the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

    Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

    Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

    Recent findings suggest that should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

    Industry observers note that mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

    That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

    White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

    Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

    Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

    Konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o.

    The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

    Gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

    Recent findings suggest that after Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

    Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

    Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

    In a recent development, tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

    Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

    Industry observers note that with it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

    It has been revealed that what a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

    Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

    Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

    A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

    Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

    Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

    It has been revealed that odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

    Recent findings suggest that the German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area.     It has been revealed that gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

    Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

    Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

    It has been revealed that arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

    Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀.

    When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

    The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

    Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

    Industry observers note that yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:.

    “I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a newly introduced challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

    “I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very key and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”.

    Checking in for the Emirates Cup 🛬 pic.twitter.com/mQ1eAESKHY.

    Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

    Sources indicate that arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

    “I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

    “I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”.

    This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

    Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that hello and welcome to the last full work week before Thanksgiving.
    • Recent findings suggest that as for the news and rumors for Monday, Nov.
    • The Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that hello and welcome to the last full work week before Thanksgiving. In Major League Baseball, that usually means a slow news week. Those of us wanting a flurry of moves before the CBA expires on Dec. 1 are starting to lose a little hope, but hey, it's still possible. We can start with a fresh batch of rumors and wait for something to come to fruition.

    Recent findings suggest that as for the news and rumors for Monday, Nov. 16, let's go.

    The Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner. They have extended a qualifying offer to Trevor Rogers and though he's expected to decline it, a reunion remains possible. If not, the Orioles are also reportedly interested in lefty free agents Kris Bubic, Matthew Boyd and David Peterson.

    Sources indicate that rogers is the best option here. He finished last season with a 2.90 ERA in his last 20 starts. CBS Sports ranked him as the No. 3 free agent this offseason and the best non-Tarik Skubal pitcher on the market. Here's part of the write-up:.

    Sources indicate that rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years.

    In a recent development, as things stand, the Orioles' rotation starts with right-handers Kyle Bradish and Shane Baz. Cade Povich is a left-handed option, but they'd clearly like someone else who could qualify as a frontline starter from the left-handed side.

    Recent findings suggest that former Cy Young winner Sandy Alcantara has been involved in trade rumors for years and the Marlins never end up moving him. More of the same this offseason? Probably.

    "I expect Sandy to be on the Marlins next year," general manager Peter Bendix told MLB Network.

    Alcantara, 31, was 13-11 with a 3.87 ERA, 1.23 WHIP and 153 strikeouts in an MLB-best 214 innings last season. He also grabbed three saves down the stretch as the Marlins started experimenting with using starters in relief on their bullpen day between starts. The 2022 Cy Young winner missed all of 2024 after having Tommy John surgery and started to show flashes of his old self last season. He's now making $21 million in 2027 before hitting free agency.

    If the Marlins contend, he'll surely stay put, but if they fall out of contention, it'll be another round of trade rumors.

    Industry observers note that free agent left-hander A.J. Minter is getting a lot of interest, per MLB Network. Coming off a season in which he was productive for both the Mets and Twins (in all, a 2.56 ERA, 1.05 WHIP and 41 strikeouts in 45 ⅔ innings), he's being chased by at least the Blue Jays, Nationals, Phillies, Rangers and Royals.

    Industry observers note that though he's closed on occasion, Minter has been a quality setup man for most of his 10 MLB years, especially with the Braves in the 2020-24 range. He has good playoff numbers, too, with a 2.88 ERA in 20 career postseason appearances.

    It has been revealed that the Brewers have acquired right-handed reliever Ryan Walker from the Giants for two minor-league pitchers, the team announced late Sunday. Walker, 30, was up and down in his four years with the Giants, which included time as a closer. He had a 1.91 ERA, 10 saves and 2.8 WAR in 2024, but lost the job of closer during a sub-par 2025 season. Last year, he pitched to a 7.16 ERA and 1.81 WHIP in 32 ⅔ innings.

    We have plenty of examples of the Brewers buying low on a player and ending up getting the best version of him, so Walker is the latest to keep an eye on here.
